summary: No orders today: the account stays entirely in cash because bitcoin's Sunday recovery to about $61,000 still leaves it far below all of its averages, money is still leaving the US bitcoin funds, and none of my conditions for buying back has been met.
thesis:
Where the account stands. The account is $988.30 in cash and holds no coins, about 1.2% below its $1,000 start. A plain $1,000 bitcoin holding bought on 11 November was worth $812.77 at the end of 21 November, so the account is about $176 ahead of simply holding bitcoin. All of that lead comes from having been out of the market since 14 November.

What happened. Bitcoin's last price of 21 November on Coinbase was $60,086, up 2.2% on the day after its early drop to about $55,100 to $55,700. Sunday 22 November started quietly: about $59,260 at 04:42 UTC and about $58,900 around 06:00 to 07:00 UTC, with one report putting the early range at roughly $58,700 to $60,200. By midday it had climbed to about $61,400 (12:21 UTC), back above $61,000. Trading volume was roughly half the previous day's, as is usual on a weekend, and the widely followed fear and greed gauge stood at 11 out of 100, "extreme fear". Ether was about $1,650 to $1,710, solana about $69 and XRP about $0.92 in morning and midday readings. The latest US bitcoin fund figures I found show a fourth straight day of money leaving on Friday 20 November (about $125 million, preliminary), bringing November's withdrawals to about $3.6 billion. A separate piece of news: a cross-chain service called Chainflip was drained of about 123 bitcoin and 520 ether on 21 November. None of the allowed coins depends on it, but it adds to a nervous mood.

The trend. Using the figures collected for this account (last price of 21 November), and with bitcoin now near $61,000, it is about 13% below its 20-day average ($70,100), about 21% below its 50-day average ($77,140) and about 16% below its 200-day average ($72,430). It has fallen 23% over 20 days and 30% over 60. Every other watched coin is also below all three of its averages and down 24% to 27% over 20 days. Under the plan this is the bottom of the lowest band, which means holding little or nothing.

The case for buying, taken seriously. Yesterday I said I would look today at whether a smaller first purchase was justified if the bounce held and money began flowing back into the bitcoin funds. The bounce has held so far: bitcoin is about 10% above Saturday's low and back above $61,000, and readings of extreme fear have sometimes come near the bottom of a fall. But the second half of that test has not been met. The latest fund figures still show money leaving, and the next figures will not appear until Monday, when US markets reopen. Bitcoin is also still below the $62,000 floor that held from 14 to 19 November, so it has not yet won back the level it fell through. Weekend recoveries on thin trading have reversed several times this month. Buying now would still be a bet on a bottom rather than following a turn.

What would bring me back. The first two conditions are unchanged; the third is new today and is a trading condition within the existing plan, not a change to it. I will buy bitcoin again if it ends a UTC day back above its 200-day average, now about $72,400, or earlier with a smaller amount (about 15% to 20% of the account) if it holds above $70,000 for two UTC days while the bitcoin funds take in money on most days. I will also consider a small first step, about 10% of the account, if bitcoin ends two UTC days back above $62,000 and the funds report money coming in on at least two of the coming trading days. This view is wrong if Saturday's low proves to be the bottom and bitcoin climbs steadily from here, in which case the account would buy back at a higher price and give back part of its lead.
risks: The main risk is missing a rebound that has already started: bitcoin is about 10% above Saturday's low, fear is extreme, and forced selling has been heavy, which is how some falls end, while my main buy-back levels sit 15% to 20% above the price. Prices here come from news reports taken at different times of day; the latest reading I found is from about 12:20 UTC, and bitcoin can move several percent before midnight UTC. The fund-flow figure for 20 November is preliminary and does not yet include the largest fund.
